entities.summary:
Nebsenra was an Egyptian pharaoh of the 14th Dynasty of Egypt during the Second Intermediate Period, reigning for a least five months over the Eastern and possibly Western Nile Delta between 1650 and 1655 BCE. He was a contemporary of the Memphis-based 13th Dynasty, with whom he shared a complex web of alliances and rivalries.

Nebsenra's reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against the Hyksos, a Semitic people who had invaded Egypt from Asia, and his efforts to reconquer the lost territories of the 13th Dynasty. Despite his efforts, Nebsenra's dynasty ultimately collapsed, and he was succeeded by a series of short-lived rulers who were eventually driven out by the Theban dynasty.

Nebsenra's legacy is that of a key figure in the tumultuous period of Second Intermediate Egypt, and his reign provides valuable insights into the complex politics and society of ancient Egypt during this period.

The discovery of Nebsenra's tomb, which has yielded a wealth of information about his reign and the culture of ancient Egypt, has provided a unique window into the past, shedding new light on the history of this enigmatic period.
